subject: science1
loDesc: Understands Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion, Universal Law of Gravitation, acceleration due to gravity (g) and its variations, Free Fall, and Escape Velocity.
hookDemo: Display a diagram of an elliptical planetary orbit around the Sun located at one focus.
hookAsk: Why does a planet speed up when it moves closer to the Sun and slow down when further away according to Kepler's second law?
streamDo: Observe physical parameters: Measured in kg, Measured in N, Scalar, Vector, Constant everywhere, Changes with location.
streamTask: Classify physical parameters under Mass versus Weight categories.
mountainTask: Calculate the gravitational force of attraction between Earth (M = 6 x 10^24 kg) and an 100 kg object on its surface (R = 6.4 x 10^6 m, G = 6.67 x 10^-11 N m^2/kg^2).
skyTask: Derive the mathematical expression for Escape Velocity v_esc = sqrt(2GM/R) = sqrt(2gr) using conservation of energy at Earth's surface and infinity.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Confusing the Universal Gravitational Constant G (constant everywhere) with local acceleration due to gravity g (varies with altitude/depth).
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Does the strength of Earth's gravity g change at the top of Mt. Everest? Does G change anywhere in the universe?'

crossCurricularLinks: Astronomy & Orbital Mechanics: Planetary Motion (Applying Kepler's elliptical area laws to satellite trajectories)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Calculates gravitational forces, analyzes variations in acceleration due to gravity, and derives escape velocity.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Use spring balances to demonstrate weight variation concepts.

subject: science1
loDesc: Traces history of periodic classification (Dobereiner Triads, Newlands Octaves, Mendeleev Periodic Table) and analyzes Modern Periodic Table trends (valency, atomic radius, metallic-nonmetallic character).
hookDemo: Display Modern Periodic Table showing s, p, d, and f blocks with highlighted metalloid zig-zag line.
hookAsk: Why does atomic radius decrease as we move from left to right across a period despite adding electrons?
streamDo: Observe atomic masses: Lithium (6.9), Sodium (23.0), Potassium (39.1).
streamTask: Verify if the atomic mass of Sodium equals the arithmetic mean of Lithium and Potassium.
mountainTask: Explain how Metallic Character changes across a Period (left to right) and down a Group (top to bottom) in the Modern Periodic Table, stating reasons.
skyTitle: Mendeleev vs Modern Periodic Table Synthesis
skyTask: Compare Mendeleev's Periodic Law (based on Atomic Mass) with Moseley's Modern Periodic Law (based on Atomic Number) and state how anomalies like isotopes were resolved.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Believing atomic radius increases across a period because additional electrons are being added.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Are the new electrons added to the same shell? What happens to nuclear charge attraction pull?' Explain radius contraction.

crossCurricularLinks: Inorganic Chemistry: Reactivity Trends (Predicting chemical bonding behavior based on group numbers and periodic trends)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Analyzes periodic classification history and investigates trends in the Modern Periodic Table.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Provide periodic table charts for students to map shell numbers across periods.

subject: science1
loDesc: Balances chemical equations, classifies reaction types (Combination, Decomposition, Displacement, Double Displacement), and investigates Exothermic/Endothermic reactions, Rate of Reaction, Oxidation, Reduction, and Redox processes.
hookDemo: Dip a clean shiny iron nail into blue Copper Sulfate (CuSO4) solution in a test tube for 15 minutes.
hookAsk: Why does the blue solution turn pale green and a reddish-brown coating form on the iron nail?
streamDo: Observe reactions: CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2, 2HgO -> 2Hg + O2, Zn + CuSO4 -> ZnSO4 + Cu, AgNO3 + NaCl -> AgCl + NaNO3.
streamTask: Classify each given reaction as Combination, Decomposition, Displacement, or Double Displacement.
mountainTask: Balance the chemical equation step-by-step: Fe + H2O -> Fe3O4 + H2.
skyTask: In the reaction CuO + H2 -> Cu + H2O, identify which substance is Oxidized, which is Reduced, the Oxidizing Agent, and the Reducing Agent.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Confusing the substance oxidized with the oxidizing agent during redox reactions.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'If hydrogen gains oxygen (is oxidized), who provided that oxygen?' The provider is the Oxidizing Agent.

crossCurricularLinks: Industrial Electrochemistry & Metallurgy: Corrosion Control (Analyzing displacement and oxidation-reduction mechanisms)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Balances chemical equations, classifies reaction types, and identifies redox mechanisms.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Perform safe displacement reaction experiments in class using zinc granules and copper sulfate.

subject: science1
loDesc: Understands heating effect of electric current (Joule's Law H = I^2 R t), electric power (P = VI), magnetic effect of electric current, Right Hand Thumb Rule, Fleming's Left Hand Rule, Fleming's Right Hand Rule, Electric Motor, and Electric Generator.
hookDemo: Display schematic cross-sections of an Electric Motor vs an Electric Generator.
hookAsk: What is the key difference between an Electric Motor (converts Electrical to Mechanical) and a Generator (converts Mechanical to Electrical)?
streamDo: Observe rules: Right Hand Thumb Rule, Fleming's Left Hand Rule, Fleming's Right Hand Rule.
streamTask: Match rules with their applications (Direction of Magnetic Field around straight wire, Direction of Force on conductor in magnetic field, Direction of Induced Current).
mountainTask: An electric iron of resistance 20 ohms takes a current of 5 A. Calculate the heat developed in 30 seconds using H = I^2 * R * t.
skyTask: Draw a schematic diagram of a DC Electric Motor and explain the role of the Split Ring Commutator in reversing current direction every half rotation.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Mixing up Fleming's Left Hand Rule (used for Electric Motors) with Fleming's Right Hand Rule (used for Electric Generators).
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Are you supplying current to get motion (Left Hand - Motor) or supplying motion to get induced current (Right Hand - Generator)?'

crossCurricularLinks: Electrical Engineering: Power Generation (Understanding industrial generator induction and split-ring commutator dynamics)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Calculates Joule heating, analyzes electromagnetic induction, and explains motor/generator mechanisms.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Build simple motor prototypes using enamel copper wire, magnets, and dry cell batteries.

subject: science1
loDesc: Investigates Latent Heat (Melting and Vaporization), Anomalous Behavior of Water using Hope's Apparatus, Dew Point, Humidity (Relative Humidity), and Specific Heat Capacity (Principle of Heat Exchange Q = m c delta T).
hookDemo: Display a graph of temperature versus time as ice at 0°C is heated continuously until it turns into steam at 100°C.
hookAsk: Why does the temperature remain constant at 0°C during melting and 100°C during boiling despite continuous heat supply?
streamDo: Observe terms: Specific Latent Heat of Fusion, Specific Latent Heat of Vaporization, Specific Heat Capacity.
streamTask: Match given terms with their correct SI units (J/kg vs J/kg.°C) and operational definitions.
mountainTask: Explain how Hope's Apparatus demonstrates the anomalous expansion of water between 0°C and 4°C, noting freezing sequence from top to bottom.
skyTask: A solid sphere of mass 100 g at 100°C is dropped into a calorimeter containing 200 g water at 20°C. Calculate final equilibrium temperature using Heat Lost = Heat Gained.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Believing that supplying heat during a phase change (like ice melting at 0°C) must always increase the temperature.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Where is the absorbed heat energy going during melting?' Explain breaking of molecular intermolecular bonds.

crossCurricularLinks: Meteorology & Environmental Physics: Aquatic Survival (Explaining marine life survival in frozen lakes via 4°C water density maximum)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Investigates latent heat, anomalous expansion of water, and calculates heat exchange using calorimetry.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Use Hope's apparatus or ice-salt freezing mixture demonstrations in class.

subject: science1
loDesc: Verifies Refraction Laws, Snell's Law (sin i / sin r = n), Refractive Index, Absolute Refractive Index, Atmospheric Refraction (twinkling stars, advanced sunrise), Dispersion of Light through prism, and Total Internal Reflection.
hookDemo: Place a glass slab on a paper sheet and shine a ray of light obliquely through one side using a laser pointer.
hookAsk: Why does the light ray bend towards the normal when entering glass from air and bend away from the normal when exiting back into air?
streamDo: Observe light ray passing: Rare to Denser medium, Denser to Rarer medium, Normal incidence (i = 0°).
streamTask: State direction of bending relative to normal for each given light ray pathway.
mountainTask: Calculate the refractive index of glass relative to air if speed of light in air is 3 x 10^8 m/s and speed in glass is 2 x 10^8 m/s (n = v1 / v2).
skyTask: Explain how a water droplet acts as a tiny glass prism to cause dispersion, total internal reflection, and refraction forming a natural rainbow.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Thinking that twinkling of stars is caused by intrinsic fluctuations in star brightness rather than atmospheric air density shifts.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Do planets twinkle? Why does point-source star light refract through changing air layers?'

crossCurricularLinks: Fiber Optics & Communication Technology: Optical Transmission (Applying total internal reflection to high-speed glass fiber cables)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Verifies Snell's law, calculates refractive index, and explains dispersion and atmospheric refraction.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Provide glass slabs, pins, and protractor sheets for student Snell's law plotting.

subject: science1
loDesc: Constructs ray diagrams for Convex and Concave lenses, applies Lens Formula (1/f = 1/v - 1/u), Magnification (m = v/u), Power of Lens (P = 1/f in meters, Diopters), Human Eye anatomy, Accommodation, and Vision Defects (Myopia, Hypermetropia, Presbyopia).
hookDemo: Display ray diagrams comparing Myopic eye (image formed in front of retina) corrected by Concave lens vs Hypermetropic eye corrected by Convex lens.
hookAsk: Why does a concave lens correct near-sightedness (myopia) while a convex lens corrects far-sightedness (hypermetropia)?
streamDo: Observe defects: Myopia (Near-sightedness), Hypermetropia (Far-sightedness), Presbyopia (Old age vision loss).
streamTask: Match vision defects with their corrective lens types (Concave, Convex, Bifocal).
mountainTask: A convex lens has a focal length of +20 cm (+0.2 m). Calculate its Optical Power in Diopters (P = 1/f) and find image distance if object is at 30 cm.
skyTask: Construct a precise ray diagram showing image formation through objective lens and eyepiece lens in a Compound Microscope.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Confusing the sign in the Lens Formula (1/f = 1/v - 1/u) with the Mirror Formula (1/f = 1/v + 1/u).
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Is there a minus sign before 1/u in the lens formula?' Remind that Lens Formula uses subtraction (1/v - 1/u).

crossCurricularLinks: Optometry & Ophthalmology: Eye Health (Calculating spectacle diopter powers to correct focal convergence defects)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Constructs lens ray diagrams, solves optics problems using lens formula, and analyzes eye vision defects.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Use optical benches with convex lenses and screen boards to map focal points.

subject: science1
loDesc: Understands physical/chemical properties of metals and non-metals, Reactivity Series of metals, Ionic Compounds, Extraction of Metals (Concentration, Roasting, Calcination, Reduction, Refining), and Corrosion prevention (Galvanization, Tinning, Anodizing, Alloying).
hookDemo: Display Reactivity Series chart ranking metals from Potassium (K - most reactive) down to Gold (Au - least reactive).
hookAsk: Why are highly reactive metals like Sodium and Aluminium extracted by electrolysis while moderately reactive metals like Zinc are extracted by carbon reduction?
streamDo: Observe ore separation processes: Hydraulic separation, Wilfley table, Froth flotation, Magnetic separation.
streamTask: Classify separation methods based on physical principle used (Density difference, Hydrophobic nature, Magnetic property).
mountainTask: Differentiate Roasting (heating sulfide ores in excess air) from Calcination (heating carbonate ores in limited air) with balanced chemical equations.
skyTask: Draw an electrolytic cell diagram for the extraction of Aluminium from purified alumina and write anode and cathode reaction equations.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Confusing Roasting (used for sulfide ores in excess air) with Calcination (used for carbonate ores in limited air).
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Does a carbonate ore already contain oxygen in CO3?' Carbonates need limited air (Calcination); sulfides need excess air (Roasting).

crossCurricularLinks: Industrial Materials & Chemistry: Ore Processing (Analyzing Hall-Heroult aluminium extraction and anti-corrosion galvanization)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Analyzes reactivity series, metallurgical extraction processes, and corrosion prevention techniques.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Perform metal reactivity displacement tests in test tubes with zinc, iron, and copper.

subject: science1
loDesc: Understands Covalent bonding in carbon, Saturated vs Unsaturated Hydrocarbons (Alkanes, Alkenes, Alkynes), Functional Groups, Homologous Series, IUPAC Nomenclature, Chemical Properties of Carbon Compounds, and Ethanol/Ethanoic Acid properties.
hookDemo: Display structural formulas for Methane (CH4), Ethene (C2H4), and Ethyne (C2H2).
hookAsk: What is the structural difference between Single (Alkane), Double (Alkene), and Triple (Alkyne) carbon-carbon covalent bonds?
streamTask: Match functional groups with their IUPAC class names (Alcohol, Aldehyde, Carboxylic Acid, Ketone, Haloalkane).
mountainTask: Write structural formulas and IUPAC names for: CH3-CH2-OH, CH3-COOH, and CH3-CH2-CH2-CHO.
skyTask: Write balanced chemical equations for Esterification (Ethanoic acid + Ethanol in presence of acid catalyst -> Ethyl ethanoate) and its reversal by Saponification.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Counting only carbon atoms in the main chain while forgetting the carbon atom inside functional groups like -CHO or -COOH.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'In CH3-COOH, how many TOTAL carbon atoms are in the chain?' Count carbon in -COOH to get ethanoic acid (2 carbons).

crossCurricularLinks: Organic & Industrial Chemistry: Polymer & Soap Manufacturing (Tracing esterification, saponification, and alcoholic fermentation)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Understands hydrocarbon classification, applies IUPAC nomenclature, and analyzes carbon compound reactions.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Use ball-and-stick molecular model kits to construct alkane/alkene chains.

subject: science1
loDesc: Understands necessity and benefits of space missions, Artificial Satellites, Satellite Launch Vehicles (SLV/PSLV), Orbits of Artificial Satellites (LEO, MEO, GEO), Orbital Velocity, and Moon/Mars Exploration Missions.
hookDemo: Display orbit diagrams showing High Earth Orbit (GEO - 35,786 km), Medium Earth Orbit (MEO - 2,000 to 35,786 km), and Low Earth Orbit (LEO - 180 to 2,000 km).
hookAsk: Why must a geostationary communication satellite be placed in High Earth Orbit at 35,786 km above Earth's equator?
streamDo: Observe satellite types: INSAT/GSAT, IRS, NAVIC, Hubble Space Telescope.
streamTask: Classify satellites based on function (Communication, Earth Observation / Remote Sensing, Navigation, Space Science).
mountainTask: Calculate critical orbital velocity v_c = sqrt(GM / (R+h)) for a satellite orbiting at height h above Earth's surface.
skyTask: Explain why satellite launch vehicles (like ISRO PSLV) use multi-stage rocket systems that drop empty fuel tanks sequentially to reduce total vehicle mass.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Believing artificial satellites float in space because there is zero gravity at LEO altitudes.
commonMisconceptions.correctionTrigger: Ask: 'Is gravity still pulling the International Space Station at 400 km?' Gravity provides centripetal force for continuous fall.

crossCurricularLinks: Aerospace & Telecommunications: ISRO Satellite Missions (Analyzing satellite orbit heights, NAVIC GPS navigation, and rocket staging)

metaNcertCode: Secondary Science LO [NCERT Secondary LO Document p. 40]
metaNcertDesc: Analyzes space mission mechanics, artificial satellite orbits, and rocket launch vehicle dynamics.
metaNishthaText: NISHTHA Module 8: Conduct water rocket or balloon rocket launch demonstrations to illustrate momentum thrust.
